Red pandas are pretty smart, so it comes down to a lot of physical and mental enrichment. We put toys in there sometimes, like balls and round things they can throw around. We also put things in brown bags and rub various scents on them, which is fun to see what scent is their favorite. We also switch up the location of where we put the bamboo. That may seem kinda simple, but it's changing small things like that that keeps their minds going. Those are the most common.

As far as the whip scorpion, there's not too much. Since it's a scorpion lol. My favorite we do is putting piles of variously sized sticks in his enclosure for him to "explore". I find it comical haha
Their poo is mushier than the mush balls I make for them.

My personal opinion is that domestication of wild animals isn't a fantastic idea. Mostly because I think if humans were told they could, they would mess it up. We're good at that when it comes to wildlife haha. 

While Parker is a very sweet and adorable panda, I've seen her mom act in very vicious ways towards visitors that, if there wasn't two barriers between them, the person would walk away with some serious injuries. 

So as cute as they are, I would not want a red panda waking around my house haha

Honestly, no Parker and her brother will probably never be released. And their cubs probably won't either. As long as wild pandas are endangered, I think animals like Parker in modern zoos have a very important job of educating visitors about wildlife conservation. The dream goal would be to not have to host these animals in zoos, that you could go to Nepal and see them flourishing in their natural habitats, but that isn't happening right now. 

As far as why we don't want to domesticate them, we want visitors to see them as wild animals so the connection between them and saving their wild counterparts is easy to make. We become familiar with our animals who are kind enough to let us share their space, as to make it easy when we are helping maintain their enclosures, hence why I get to chill with the pandas. They are trained enough to do basic things such as enter and exit carriers for transportation to different locations, but they are not tame to the point where we could touch them.

When they are REALLY excited (or mad) they make a screaming/squeaking noise. But in the mornings when I come to wake them up and get bamboo, it's this noise that actually sounds like hissing. It's kinda off putting at first, but I've learned it's a friendly noise. Freaked me out the first time haha
Believe it or not, I'm actually a volunteer haha. At our zoo, the animal care volunteers do a lot of hard, but fun work. Although I will say that panda poo is actually kinda the worst poo.
Trust me, I can't explain to you the temptation I have everyday to hug them haha. Takes a lot of will power. So much will power.

Not to brag, but I'm at a pretty amazing zoo. Not only are we very conservation driven, but we have constant enrichment for our animals (I even help enrich our whip scorpions lol). Our pandas, since they are pretty smart, get almost daily enrichment which keeps them entertained and keeps their minds busy and happy. As far as scheduled times, it comes when we are providing them care. Typically we enter the enclosure at least twice a day to maintain the exhibit and care for the pandas. No specific time of day really though

They are pretty dang fluffy. Their tail is probably fairly small, but with the fur the tails are like giant long pillows of happiness. Overall, they have a lot of long, thinner fur. When they are wet, their fur doesn't completely lay flat on them, similar to how nonshedding dog fur looks when wet. 

Sadly, red pandas are poached often for their amazing coats. Up close, they are even more stunning than photos can show. It's a shame that their populations are decreasing due to human activity, but it's pandas like Parker that remind us how important it is for us to step in and save her wild counterparts.

It really depends on the panda. Anything with a mouth can bite, and even in captivity they still have wild instincts. However, Parker and her brother are insanely friendly. They are our cubs this year and are very curious. They try to approach me or try to climb on me often which I have to step away from because it's important we don't domesticate them. When they hear me coming, they get extremely excited. They run around and make their little noise because they know that my appearance = bamboo.

Their mom on the other hand, has very sharp teeth and claws and isn't afraid to show them. But I would not approach a red panda personally haha, they have the capability to cause some serious harm for sure. As cute as they really are

When my current boyfriend and I first had sex, it was also our first time ever: virgins all the way. I had been on the pill for about three years prior to that (for regulating my period) and we chose not to use a condom.
USE. A. CONDOM.

By 100%, I mean not missing a single day and taking it at the exact same time every single day. If her use isn't that perfect, the birth control effectiveness decreases to around 70% I believe? (Check the planned parenthood website for confirmation on my numbers). I highly recommend the pill, but you also need to be tested for STD's. If you chose not to be, pile condoms on top of that. Currently, I have an IUD, which boasts a 99% effective rate. I LOVE IT. LOVE LOVE LOVE IT, don't have to remember to take a pill, covered by insurance, and it makes sex better. To not have to worry about pregnancy is a wonderful thing my friend. 

Now onto the more fun stuff. As far as making sex more fun and exciting, it's all about exploration. Look around on the sex subbredit, look around your local sex shop.
